hardware.board: NVIDIA Jetson AGX Thor Developer Kit

cold_start.caveat: weights_cached=true - total_s excludes any download, and is not comparable with a first-pull cold start. Component resolution is bounded by the ~2s health-poll interval.

memory.kv_cache_bytes_per_token_formula: 2 x 28 layers x 4 kv_heads x 128 head_dim x 2 bytes = 57344 B/token (KV dtype: auto -> model dtype)
memory.peak_device_source: nvidia-smi --query-compute-apps, summed over every compute process, sampled through the whole server session
memory.breakdown_note: the runtime itemises 46.2 GiB of the 47.2 GiB the driver reports resident; the 1.0 GiB residual is CUDA context, library workspaces and allocator slack, which no backend breaks out
memory.board_accounting_caveat: These board-level figures do NOT attribute this config's footprint and must not be used as if they did. 55.2 GB of this Tegra is invisible to /proc/meminfo (the GPU carveout), and the NVIDIA driver's pool does not shrink when a server exits - so a run against a warm pool shows almost no rise. Measured 2026-09-11: a session that allocated 14.25 GiB of weights moved board `used` by 4.5 GiB, and tegrastats agreed with that wrong number because it measures the same quantity. Use peak_device_bytes.

max_context.search_tolerance_note: binary search stopped once the bracket closed to 256 tokens, so the true limit lies in [16161, 16384); the reported value is the largest prompt VERIFIED to complete, never an extrapolation
max_context.limiting_factor: configuration (the server's own declared context limit, not memory)
max_context.failure_detail: {"error":{"message":"This model's maximum context length is 16384 tokens. However, you requested 1 output tokens and your prompt contains at least 16384 input tokens, for a total of at least 16385 tokens. Please reduce the length of the input prompt or the number of requested output tokens. (parameter=input_tokens, value=16384)","type":"BadRequestError","param":"input_tokens","code":400}}

prefix_caching_disabled.method: second identical request timed against the first, per cell, on a prompt with a unique leading token

board_quiet.method: assert_condition_matches_reality(): no other containers and no bare-metal process holding an nvhost/nvgpu/nvmap handle

warmups_discarded.method: warmed up to a MEASURED steady state per cell, not to a fixed count: at least --warmup-min-s under load plus a stability check on recent decode rates. Written to records.jsonl with phase='warmup' and excluded by analysis/stats.py, which reads only phase='measure'

identical_prompt_bytes_within_run.method: every repetition of a cell sends one frozen corpus string; its sha256 is on every record row

greedy_decode.caveat: temperature alone is NOT controlled sampling - the three backends apply different top_p/top_k/min_p defaults (Edge-LLM 0.9/50, vLLM 1.0/-1). This run pins temperature only; the greedy control that pins top_k=1 is a separate experiment.

seed._not_collected: no seed is sent; at temperature=0 the sampler is deterministic anyway, but this is an assertion about the backend, not a verification

max_tokens_and_stop.value: max_tokens=128, no stop sequences on any backend

prefix_caching_request_field.caveat: sent on every request where the backend's prompt cache is a request-level setting (llama-server's cache_prompt); inert elsewhere. Verified by the cache probe, not by this field.

prefix_caching_flag.caveat: a launch flag, believed; the verification is the cache probe above

gpu_offload.caveat: llama.cpp only; -1 means all layers. Verified against the server's own 'offloaded N/M layers' log line in memory.offloaded_layers

fan_profile._not_collected: not read; /sys/devices/pwm-fan is not exposed on this L4T build and no fan profile was pinned for this run

not_yet_verified.identical_rendered_prompt_bytes_across_f: asserted by construction - all frameworks send the same corpus string - but the RENDERED prompt (after each backend's chat template) is not compared in this run. scripts/chat_template_crossfeed.py did exactly that comparison for vLLM vs Edge-LLM on BFCL and found byte equality; it has not been re-run for this corpus.
